tool_args.rationale: All observations already match the target horizon of 0.6. The remaining ambiguity is whether suppression changes smoothly or engages only when input and gradient jointly enter a particular regime. The trajectory batch is the remaining relevant probe for resolving that ambiguity before confirmation.

considered_alternatives.option: Saturating base with smooth sink suppression
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The low-gradient rows constrain the base, but the remaining rows vary input and gradient together. A smooth sink and a gated sink can explain the observed deficits yet give different forecasts.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit a conjunctive sink gate now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The six rows do not independently bracket the input and gradient thresholds, so fitting the gate now could put the branch boundary in the wrong place.
The acquired row anchors the low-gradient branch; another measurement there would not resolve where the sink engages.
